title: MADGER World Bible
status: Present-day development complete for this edition; origins and wider-world history explicitly reserved for the next phase.
premise: The Burrow is one busy, welcoming town with populated outdoor terraces and a larger underground neighborhood network. People move between both every day. If the outdoor district is overrun, an independent inner boundary protects the inhabited underground town.

scope.included: The existing outdoor basin, populated underground levels, their public/service/egress connections and normal/protected operating states.
scope.excluded: Undefined exterior lands, attacker identity, a finished game implementation and real-world structural/mechanical engineering.

authority_order: This World Bible and its matching versioned map data
Location/model sheets checked against this Bible
Individual episode, game and promotional assets

retained: Four established heroes and character/voice corrections
Warm, prosperous settlement and gradual clues
Sunwell, west workshops, north gardens, south homes, east bridge/gate
Independent physical gate bar and local digital records
new_in_this_edition: Five neighborhood identities and eight recurring resident dossiers.
Seven measured sub-locations inside existing allocated rooms.
Present-day civic life, routines, culture and bounded story possibilities.
Owner establishes Madger as founder; reasons and historical sequence remain reserved.
BRW-13 role wording aligned with the already established public daytime gate state.
supersedes: R6 schematic geography where it lacks precise dimensions
R6 shots showing a road beyond the gate
Lantern/Warden pilot plot and arbitrary architectural changes
Surface-only scope, approximate 400-person planning population and closed-gate default from v1.0.0.
Pilot requirements that the public gate remain closed in every daytime shot.

geography.origin: Sunwell center at finished market paving level
geography.perimeter: Ellipse x^2/300^2 + y^2/220^2 = 1 is the planning boundary. Render rock as irregular inside this envelope without moving anchors.
geography.inside_definition: The Burrow includes the outdoor basin and inhabited chambers beneath it and its inner rock terraces. Episode 1 can show both, but not the unassigned exterior beyond the east boundary.
geography.scale_policy: Coordinates and anchored footprints are fixed production layout. Local decoration and rock texture vary only within their allocated bounds. Roof heights and building shell details remain production specifications, not surveyed real-world engineering.

population_plan.basis: New production planning baseline, not a user-specified census. Four residential wards of 100 homes at an average four residents; shared services support both districts.

geography.underground_section: Occupied room floors are -12 m and -24 m. Services are -36 m. Typical drawn chamber clear height is 6 m; the section reserves intervening rock. These are fictional production dimensions, not verified structural calculations.

canon_rules.title: One shared place
canon_rules.rule: Every episode, game hub and story illustration references the same location IDs, compass directions, routes and landmark relationships.

canon_rules.title: Permanent base, recorded change
canon_rules.rule: Geography and built footprints form the baseline. Weather, repairs, new occupants and event damage belong in dated state overlays. Growth adds entries; it does not silently redraw the base.

canon_rules.title: Inside means inside
canon_rules.rule: Episode 1 stays within the outdoor basin and mapped underground town. An open public gate may be shown from an inward-facing angle without depicting the undefined exterior. No villain or exterior attack cutaway.

canon_rules.title: Care has ordinary causes
canon_rules.rule: Food, water, repairs and safety come from neighbors and working infrastructure. No magic lantern, universal energy core, or secretly indispensable hero sustains the town.

canon_rules.title: Trust can be checked
canon_rules.rule: A message is evidence of a report, not proof that an event occurred. Digital, physical and personal observations can disagree.

canon_rules.title: The four remain themselves
canon_rules.rule: Madger, Gorilla White, MADGER Bot and Snow White retain their established designs and approved voices. Snow has canine sounds only. No duplicate hero mascots as anonymous crowd fillers.

canon_rules.title: The pilot earns its warmth
canon_rules.rule: Show skill, generosity, play and ordinary friction before clues. No pilot attack, named villain reveal or retroactive sabotage of the repaired bridge.

canon_rules.title: No convenience architecture
canon_rules.rule: A chase may use an existing route or a newly documented extension. It cannot conjure a door through a previously solid wall or change which side of the canal a building occupies.

canon_rules.title: Same environment, different presentation
canon_rules.rule: Anime may use painted linework and game assets may use 3D meshes. Their scale, silhouettes, sign placement, doors and travel connections agree.

canon_rules.title: Unknown is not permission to improvise
canon_rules.rule: External lands, undisclosed tunnels and unnamed NPC biographies remain unassigned. Define and record them before using them as plot facts.

canon_rules.title: One town above and below
canon_rules.rule: Both parts are highly populated permanent neighborhoods. Underground living is normal and valued; its residents share surface civic life.

canon_rules.title: Welcome first, independent defense
canon_rules.rule: Public entrance is open in normal life. The inhabited underground town has a separate, more defensible inner boundary. Account for main, service and emergency ingress; no bypass invented for convenience.

canon_rules.title: People before closure
canon_rules.rule: Defensive state changes retain civilian refuge, manual egress, air, water and local control. A status message alone cannot operate the physical gate bar.

canon_rules.title: A plan for every area
canon_rules.rule: Register a blueprint, fixed coordinates and connections before a new area appears. New districts extend this world; event damage does not silently redraw its baseline.

locations.name: Sunwell Market
locations.role: The civic center: daily exchange, news and informal decisions.
anchors: Round limestone well curb at the world origin; sealed potable-water draw point, never an energy core.
Four dark inset paving rays mark north, east, south and west.
Green canvas stalls occupy the north and west edges; the east route stays clear.
A freestanding timber noticeboard stands at (18,20,0).
doors: Open east to Gate Lane, south to Hearth Lane, west to Workshop Lane and north to Garden Way.
locations.daily_life: Produce arrives before breakfast. Neighbors trade repairs, food and information. A returned tool matters as much as a sale.
locations.story_use: Let the community solve ordinary problems here. A future false notice has recognizable recipients and consequences.
locations.game_use: Home hub, dialogue, noticeboard quests and map orientation. No random hazards in the peaceful baseline.
continuity_limits: Keep the center open. Stalls move only within marked bays. Never mirror the paving compass or move the well.

locations.name: Common House & Tables
locations.role: A communal kitchen, shared meal room and meeting place open to the market.
anchors: Long north-facing porch; three permanent stone table bases in its forecourt.
Warm plaster, green shutters, copper kitchen vent on the southwest corner.
Four friends usually sit at the eastern porch table; it is not privately reserved.
doors: Main double doors centered in the north wall.
Kitchen service door in west wall.
Second exit in southeast corner.
locations.daily_life: Households have their own kitchens. This kitchen serves workers, visitors and shared meals; no one must earn food through heroics.
locations.story_use: The emotional home of the pilot and a repeatable place for disagreements, apologies and celebrations.
locations.game_use: Rest, party conversations and meal preparation. Healing/rest is a game interaction, not instant story-world magic.
continuity_limits: Do not turn the forecourt into a different plaza. Seasonal cloths and food are state changes.

locations.name: Hearth Terraces
locations.role: The principal residential neighborhood, built into the southern rock.
anchors: Three inhabited tiers at +6, +12 and +18 metres.
Pale stone lower walls, dark timber balconies, slate roofs and individual colored doors.
Madger and Snow share the ground-level accessible home entry at the west end of the +12 m terrace.
doors: Each dwelling opens to a public gallery.
Stairs shorten the route; the western switchback ramp reaches every occupied tier.
locations.daily_life: Laundry, school bags, meals, repairs and quiet hours make this a neighborhood rather than a backdrop.
locations.story_use: Private thresholds give friendships boundaries. Residents have plans independent of the heroes.
locations.game_use: Home save point and optional conversations. Occupied homes are not loot containers.
continuity_limits: This edition fixes neighborhood massing and Madger/Snow entry, not every unseen room or every resident name.

locations.name: Garden Terraces
locations.role: North terraces for produce, plant starts and shared learning.
anchors: Three broad planted bands at +6, +12 and +18 metres.
Two low greenhouses sit at the eastern end of the +12 m terrace.
Garden crossing BRW-C02 links the lower path to Garden Way.
doors: South stair from Garden Way.
Long west ramp for carts and mobility access.
locations.daily_life: Growers share water schedules. Greens, roots and fruit supplement traded grain; gardens do not magically feed everyone alone.
locations.story_use: A future changed delivery schedule can cause a missed watering without threatening the whole town at once.
locations.game_use: Cultivation, observation and soil-route tutorials in designated beds only.
continuity_limits: No new cliff or waterfall between tiers. North remains north in every season.

locations.name: Spring House
locations.role: Protected source, settling tanks and the start of separate water systems.
anchors: Low limestone vault built into the northwest wall.
Three labeled valve wheels inside; a fenced settling court outside.
Drinking-water tanks are covered; the utility race is visibly separate.
doors: South inspection entrance from Garden Ramp.
locations.daily_life: A water team checks clarity and flow physically and records the result before opening the daily allocation.
locations.story_use: Careful work becomes familiar before any later attempt to falsify it.
locations.game_use: Inspection puzzles and valve routing with a local effect; never a universal town-off switch.
continuity_limits: No bathing or dumping in potable tanks. Water flows downhill along fixed routes.

locations.name: Waterhouse
locations.role: Water-driven power and maintenance beside the western wheelrace.
anchors: One 6 m diameter vertical waterwheel on the east wall.
Separate mechanical sluice and electrical isolator.
Wheelrace runs on the building's east side; the workshop stands south.
doors: South door to the workshop court.
West equipment door to perimeter service path.
locations.daily_life: Operators clean grates and compare local gauges; nearby roofs add solar power and local batteries.
locations.story_use: Local consequences create practical rescue and repair stories later.
locations.game_use: Environmental repair and supervised mechanisms. No unrestricted control of the entire settlement.
continuity_limits: The wheel never migrates to the gate or north gardens. Power and drinking water remain independent.

locations.name: Gorilla White's Workshop
locations.role: A public repair workshop where Gorilla White works alongside other craftspeople.
anchors: Wide east-facing pair of timber doors.
Big shared bench beneath north windows; blue tool silhouettes on the west rack.
A small private rest alcove is behind the south partition, never in the public tool aisle.
doors: East workshop doors to the court.
North service door to Waterhouse.
South door to the western walk.
locations.daily_life: Repair tickets are public. Apprentices do real work. Gorilla accepts help and takes turns being off duty.
locations.story_use: Repairs reveal community relationships; strength can support rather than replace other people.
locations.game_use: Upgrade station, craft tasks and companion conversation. Purchases do not rewrite plot outcomes.
continuity_limits: No weapon factory in the peaceful baseline. Shelves may gain tools; walls and doors stay fixed.

locations.name: Training Court
locations.role: A safe, open practice yard with marked soil lanes and rescue exercises.
anchors: Low timber boundary on three sides; east entrance stays open.
Two sand/soil strips, reusable wooden obstacles and a rope-rescue frame.
Soft soil lane A runs north-south inside the court; buried utilities are outside its bounds.
doors: East public entrance from the lower ring walk.
North equipment gate toward workshop.
locations.daily_life: Children practice coordination; adults rehearse carrying and rescue. Training is scheduled around rest hours.
locations.story_use: A place for effort, humor, failure and gradual competence before a real emergency.
locations.game_use: Jump, guard and BURROW tutorials. Down/S/down-swipe/BURROW retain their established behavior.
continuity_limits: Digging is allowed only in defined soil volumes; never phase through stone, homes or pipes.

locations.name: Records House
locations.role: Bot's workroom, local records and the room where evidence is compared.
anchors: Slate-blue shutters and copper cable trays.
A public counter at the south; comparison table in the center.
Offline records cabinet at the north; Bot's charging dock at the northeast.
doors: South public entrance.
East maintenance door.
locations.daily_life: People can correct records and ask how a decision was made. Bot helps; he does not own everyone's information.
locations.story_use: An uncertain observation can be preserved without becoming an accusation.
locations.game_use: Quest journal, evidence board and local electronics tasks. Story knowledge and player discoveries are separate states.
continuity_limits: No all-seeing surveillance wall or omniscient AI. The pilot does not name an attacker.

locations.name: Storehouse & Trading Court
locations.role: Dry staples, tools and an interior receiving yard.
anchors: Long green double doors on the east.
Raised dry floor, numbered shelves, reusable D-series delivery tags.
Receiving court on the east is broad enough to turn a handcart.
doors: East cart entrance.
North staff door toward Gate Lane.
West inventory exit.
locations.daily_life: Outside trade supplies grain, cloth and spare parts. The shared reserve buffers interruptions; households keep personal supplies.
locations.story_use: A missing crate means a specific repair or meal is delayed. Outsiders are not automatically suspicious.
locations.game_use: Supplies, delivery errands and restoration materials. No invented real-money reward economy.
continuity_limits: D17 is a delivery identifier, not a prophecy, secret emblem or villain's name.

locations.name: Care House
locations.role: A quiet neighborhood clinic and recovery space.
anchors: Cream shutters, a simple blue circle sign and a planted waiting porch.
Two rest rooms behind the reception area.
doors: North accessible entrance.
West service exit.
locations.daily_life: Ordinary checkups, rest and help for injuries; care does not depend on game rank.
locations.story_use: Consequences and recovery have a place, without turning every danger into spectacle.
locations.game_use: Recovery and rescue handoff. Actual story injuries follow the event ledger.
continuity_limits: Do not replace it with a prison, armory or secret lab without an explicit canon revision.

locations.name: East Bridge
locations.role: The main public crossing between Gate Lane and the interior arrival court.
anchors: 12 m east-west deck over a 6 m north-south canal; low stone abutments.
Pale repaired timber, waist-high simple rails, three modest green pennants for the reopening.
No overhead structure and no chasm.
doors: West landing at x=164.
East landing at x=176.
locations.daily_life: Carts and pedestrians take turns on the crossing. Service Crossing provides a bypass during maintenance.
locations.story_use: A shared accomplishment in Episode 1, repaired after ordinary seasonal weather.
locations.game_use: Landmark, route choice and later defense position. Fixed geometry in every mode.
continuity_limits: No collapse, sabotage reveal or large arched stone replacement in the pilot.

locations.name: Inner Arrival Court
locations.role: An internal handoff space between East Bridge and the public gate vestibule.
anchors: Open paved court, shaded waiting bench on the north and two marked cart bays.
Delivery bell and small green status display beside the gate approach.
Visitors and deliveries are welcome in ordinary life. Pilot shots stay on interior ground and look inward.
doors: West toward bridge.
East into the internal gate vestibule.
South into Service Walk.
locations.daily_life: A gate steward receives visitors and compares paper tags with the local record.
locations.story_use: Show hospitality and careful procedure together. One duplicate receipt quietly contradicts a simple count.
locations.game_use: Arrival/tutorial staging and visitor interactions without exposing undefined exterior terrain.
continuity_limits: No view past the exterior threshold in Episode 1.

locations.name: East Gate
locations.role: A recessed gate vestibule and the main public threshold at the east rock wall.
anchors: Twin timber-and-iron gate leaves at x=294.
Mechanical crossbar on the inside, independent of the arrival log; disengaged when the public gate is open.
Inner relay cabinet BRW-15 is on the south wall: the right wall when facing outward/east.
Vestibule mouth at x=270 opens into the arrival court.
doors: Exterior leaf plane stays at x=294. Public passage is open during ordinary daytime. The pilot uses inward framing; no unassigned exterior landscape is shown.
Vestibule west mouth remains x=270. Leaves may close routinely at night or under an explicit protective state.
locations.daily_life: Staff open and close it; electronics record observations and schedules, not physical permission by themselves.
locations.story_use: The same visible bar, leaves and cabinet make the last unexplained receipt legible.
locations.game_use: Future adventure boundary; locked by the current quest state, not by an invented wall across the market.
continuity_limits: Do not confuse the outdoor public gate with the new underground inner gates. Normal hospitality and defensive readiness coexist.

locations.name: Service Walk & Gate Relay
locations.role: Public maintenance access along the inner south side of the gate.
anchors: Slate paving, one shallow drain and one inspection hatch at (264,-26,0).
Cabinet R-E01 mounted at (282,-8.5,1.2), on the vestibule's south wall.
Cabinet door is flush and intact in the pilot; its display uses ordinary muted green.
doors: North access from arrival court; return through the west vestibule mouth to reach the cabinet on its inner south wall.
No shortcut through the solid south vestibule wall.
locations.daily_life: Maintenance is scheduled and logged. The place is mundane before Snow notices an unfamiliar trace.
locations.story_use: A held indication and recorded time create a question; the source remains unknown.
locations.game_use: Inspection, local relay isolation and evidence comparisons in later missions.
continuity_limits: Never move the cabinet to the north wall. Never imply Snow can smell a digital hack.

locations.name: Makers' Room & Archive
locations.role: A shared studio, reading room and record of community projects.
anchors: Ochre door facing south, long north worktable and east archive wall.
Displayed objects have credited makers and recorded histories.
doors: South public entrance.
West service exit.
locations.daily_life: Neighbors draw, record stories, learn skills and mend small objects. Celebrations add dated artifacts.
locations.story_use: A living memory of past adventures without inventing ancient prophecy.
locations.game_use: Creator Studio and Trophy Chamber functions share this building; neither becomes an extra wing by accident.
continuity_limits: No unrecorded trophy from an adventure the characters have not had.

locations.name: Hearth Public Entry
locations.role: A welcoming gallery below the Hearth Terraces. Public doors at (-30,-100,0) lead to lifts/stairs landing in the Welcome Hall. A continuous ramp provides a powered-lift-independent route.
continuity_limits: Public in ordinary life. Entry is a civic threshold, not a private club or a token-holder gate.

locations.name: Welcome Hall
locations.role: The underground arrival hall: visitor information, seating, stroller/cart space and a steward desk. All main-entry routes arrive here before the inner boundary.
continuity_limits: Queue space remains before the two inner closures. No lift or ramp may discharge directly behind the inner gates.

locations.name: Inner Gate Gallery
locations.role: A broad civic passage with two independently operated inner closures. Both are open on ordinary days.
continuity_limits: Closure lines at y=-144 and y=-128 protect the town beyond. Staff confirm people are clear; no automatic trapping of a crowded passage.

locations.name: Underhall Commons
locations.role: A busy indoor high street with everyday shops, shared tables, a meeting square and neighborhood directions.
continuity_limits: The central circulation cross stays open. This is a daily public place, not an empty bunker.

locations.name: West Lantern Warren
locations.role: Four household courts, shared play rooms, deliveries, doorways, kitchens and quiet residential galleries. Planning occupancy: 400 residents / 100 homes.
continuity_limits: Lantern is a neighborhood name and ordinary lighting; no magical energy object. Private room layouts stay unassigned until drawn.

locations.name: East Orchard Warren
locations.role: Four dense residential courts with family homes, planted gathering pockets and neighbor-run shops. Planning occupancy: 400 residents / 100 homes.
continuity_limits: Plants are decorative and locally grown; they do not imply unlimited daylight or a self-feeding town.

locations.name: School & Play Hall
locations.role: Classrooms, reading, supervised play, making and community learning used by children from both surface and underground homes.
continuity_limits: Children retain ordinary routines and protected gathering areas; danger does not turn the school into a combat room.

locations.name: Care & Community Hall
locations.role: Clinic rooms, recovery, community meals and a separate kitchen wing, with independent clean and service circulation.
continuity_limits: Clinical rooms remain private. Kitchen noise and deliveries stay outside the care-room aisle.

locations.name: Central Lift & Stair Court
locations.role: A stacked neighborhood interchange at -12, -24 and -36 m, with ordinary lifts and independent stairs.
continuity_limits: This core has no direct surface entrance. It connects only the protected side of the underground town.

locations.name: Service Receiving Hall
locations.role: Freight from the workshop service passage is checked, staged and handed into the west neighborhood through a local closure.
continuity_limits: The dock gate is a separate surface-to-town defensive boundary; it cannot be left as an unguarded bypass.

locations.name: West Deep Warren
locations.role: A second residential neighborhood, equal in dignity and quality to the upper warren. Planning occupancy: 400 residents / 100 homes.
continuity_limits: Depth is not a class hierarchy. These residents use surface gardens, markets and celebrations daily.

locations.name: East Deep Warren
locations.role: Dense family courtyards, homes, doorstep shops and social galleries on the second inhabited level. Planning occupancy: 400 residents / 100 homes.
continuity_limits: The four wards are normal permanent homes, not temporary emergency beds.

locations.name: Deep Commons & Kitchens
locations.role: A shared meal hall, neighborhood shops and kitchens beside the lower residential streets.
continuity_limits: Keep food preparation, clean stores and waste handling distinct. Household kitchens also exist.

locations.name: Food Gardens & Grow Rooms
locations.role: Powered growing rooms, seed storage and food preparation for selected greens, herbs and plant starts.
continuity_limits: Grow lights require power. Underground cultivation supplements surface gardens and external trade; it does not feed everybody alone.

locations.name: Assembly & Refuge Hall
locations.role: Used daily for gatherings, sport, performances and clubs. In a protective state it receives surface residents, with rest, care and family reunification zones.
continuity_limits: 800 additional refuge places is a production planning target, not a certified capacity. Do not displace underground households to make refuge space.

locations.name: Baths & Laundry
locations.role: Shared baths, private washing rooms, laundry, drying and neighborhood maintenance stores.
continuity_limits: Separate clean water from drainage. No connection opens through the Welcome Hall above.

locations.name: Utility Repair Hall
locations.role: Maintainable local power distribution, battery rooms, spare equipment and repair benches.
continuity_limits: Separate zones can be isolated. A failure here cannot be written as an unexplained instant shutdown of all life support.

locations.name: Water & Air Service Rooms
locations.role: Partitioned potable reserve, wastewater lift plant, drainage sumps and air-handling rooms.
continuity_limits: Wastewater must be pumped up to the existing -3 m service level; it cannot flow uphill by gravity. Independent duty/backup equipment and local controls.

locations.name: Deep Stores
locations.role: Dry staples, household supplies, repair materials and documented community reserves.
continuity_limits: Stock quantities change in the event ledger. No infinite supplies or unearned emergency solution.

locations.name: West Stair & Refuge Core
locations.role: An independent protected stair/refuge core links all three underground levels to the surface service walk at (-210,-40,0).
continuity_limits: Outside entry is locally controlled. Occupants can leave from inside without network permission; surface conditions still determine whether evacuation is safe.

locations.name: East Stair & Refuge Core
locations.role: A second separated protected stair/refuge core links all levels to the surface service walk at (144,-40,0).
continuity_limits: This is a distinct route from the west core. Include it in any surface-overrun state and keep staff able to operate it locally.

water.headrace: The first two segments are enclosed under the western garden ramp. The open wheelrace begins on the east side of Waterhouse at (-161,65).
water.potable: Covered spring tanks feed separate buried drinking-water pipes; no sewage, wheelrace water or garden runoff enters this system.
water.wastewater: Sealed collection lines run under service paths to a treatment room in the southeast rock; outflow is distinct from potable and irrigation systems.
water.surface_water: Storm drains and garden overflow enter a screened lower outlet. Canal edges near public paths have continuous simple rails.
water.maintenance: Manual isolation at each branch; log a local failure as local, with a visible fallback.

heroes.name: Madger
heroes.place: Sunwell, Common House and the shared home at Hearth Terraces
heroes.role: Organizer, explorer and friend; not the ruler.
heroes.design: Established black-and-cream design, black belly, high cream chest V, natural arms and small even teeth. Clean face; no decorative tear, sweat streak or oversized fang.
heroes.strength: Initiative, courage and a talent for bringing people together.
heroes.flaw: Mistakes taking every job for being dependable.
heroes.pilot: Accepts a neighbor's plan, shares the work, gives away credit and stops to listen to Snow.
heroes.long_arc: Learns that leadership means building a capable community, including disagreement and checks on his own judgment.
heroes.game: BURROW is a physical movement through designated soil, with a visible entry, dirt trail and emergence.

heroes.name: Gorilla White
heroes.place: Workshop, Waterhouse, bridge and common tables
heroes.role: Craftsperson and protector; not an unlimited force.
heroes.design: Approved white/tan fur and blue eyes; preserve established body proportions.
heroes.strength: Patience, strength, workmanship and an instinct to shield others.
heroes.flaw: Carries the burden alone until everyone mistakes his endurance for invulnerability.
heroes.pilot: Lets neighbors help and sits down for the meal.
heroes.long_arc: Builds others' skill and trusts a team to protect him as well as the town.
heroes.game: Guard, rescue and safe support; no infinite saves or casual demolition of the home map.

heroes.name: MADGER Bot
heroes.place: Records House, relay cabinets and maintenance routes
heroes.role: Systems keeper and evidence partner; not an omniscient administrator.
heroes.design: Entirely mechanical face/visor and established metallic body; no fur muzzle, human skin or fang.
heroes.strength: Memory, method and a sincere wish to make daily life easier.
heroes.flaw: Feels that being useful requires having a definite answer.
heroes.pilot: Keeps the duplicate receipt and admits that its cause is not yet known.
heroes.long_arc: Trusts independent observation, states uncertainty and protects people without taking over their decisions.
heroes.game: Local electronics, evidence comparison and established boosts; bounded access and visible feedback.

heroes.name: Snow White
heroes.place: Shared home, common tables, training yard and walks with the team
heroes.role: Adult quadrupedal shepherd, companion and scout; a real dog.
heroes.design: Approved adult shepherd form with rose collar; stable four-legged anatomy. Canine sounds only.
heroes.strength: Scent, hearing, attention, affection and decisive physical action.
heroes.flaw: An exciting sensation can pull her ahead before others understand.
heroes.pilot: Stops, looks back and holds an indication until Madger joins her.
heroes.long_arc: Develops reliable teamwork through indication, return and restraint; does not gain human speech.
heroes.game: Established companion support and physical threat response. She detects a physical trace, never a digital packet.

episode_1.beat: Open with an underground household preparing breakfast, children on the common street and neighbors moving up to the sunlit market. Introduce all four heroes through useful, ordinary actions.
episode_1.boundary: All views remain in the Burrow; show above and below as one everyday town.
episode_1.clue: None. The first impression is warm, crowded, safe and capable.

episode_1.beat: A visitor is welcomed and a delivery is counted. The main underground route passes through open inner gates with residents moving both directions.
episode_1.boundary: Frame toward interior space. Do not turn the inner gate into a threat reveal.
episode_1.clue: One duplicate D17 receipt; Bot preserves both without accusation.

episode_1.beat: Neighbors reopen the weather-repaired bridge. Gorilla accepts help, Madger shares credit and underground residents join the celebration.
episode_1.boundary: Time cuts preserve actual travel distances.
episode_1.clue: No sabotage, attacker or extra bridge.

episode_1.beat: Show learning, shared food and the ordinary use of both districts. After a time cut, Snow holds an indication near the intact gate relay; Madger pays attention.
episode_1.boundary: Snow notices an unfamiliar physical trace, never a digital hack by scent.
episode_1.clue: Source unknown; no forced connection to the duplicate receipt.

episode_1.beat: End the day with friends and households returning home above and below. Bot retains the observations and plans a careful check.
episode_1.boundary: A brief routine evening gate closing can be shown without alarm.
episode_1.clue: The community stays joyful; the audience has a small unresolved question.

episode_1.beat: After the documented routine closing, the local log receives another D17 acknowledgment although no new passage occurred.
episode_1.boundary: Inward shot of the closed outdoor leaves; no outside silhouette or villain.
episode_1.clue: An unexplained discrepancy, not proof of a cause or attack.

expansion.version_policy: PATCH corrects wording without changing canon; MINOR adds compatible places/people/events; MAJOR records an owner-authorized retcon. Never overwrite the previous meaning silently.

areas.name: Hearth Public Entry
areas.role: A welcoming gallery below the Hearth Terraces. Public doors at (-30,-100,0) lead to lifts/stairs landing in the Welcome Hall. A continuous ramp provides a powered-lift-independent route.
continuity_limits: Public in ordinary life. Entry is a civic threshold, not a private club or a token-holder gate.

areas.name: Welcome Hall
areas.role: The underground arrival hall: visitor information, seating, stroller/cart space and a steward desk. All main-entry routes arrive here before the inner boundary.
continuity_limits: Queue space remains before the two inner closures. No lift or ramp may discharge directly behind the inner gates.

areas.name: Inner Gate Gallery
areas.role: A broad civic passage with two independently operated inner closures. Both are open on ordinary days.
continuity_limits: Closure lines at y=-144 and y=-128 protect the town beyond. Staff confirm people are clear; no automatic trapping of a crowded passage.

areas.name: Underhall Commons
areas.role: A busy indoor high street with everyday shops, shared tables, a meeting square and neighborhood directions.
continuity_limits: The central circulation cross stays open. This is a daily public place, not an empty bunker.

areas.name: West Lantern Warren
areas.role: Four household courts, shared play rooms, deliveries, doorways, kitchens and quiet residential galleries. Planning occupancy: 400 residents / 100 homes.
continuity_limits: Lantern is a neighborhood name and ordinary lighting; no magical energy object. Private room layouts stay unassigned until drawn.

areas.name: East Orchard Warren
areas.role: Four dense residential courts with family homes, planted gathering pockets and neighbor-run shops. Planning occupancy: 400 residents / 100 homes.
continuity_limits: Plants are decorative and locally grown; they do not imply unlimited daylight or a self-feeding town.

areas.name: School & Play Hall
areas.role: Classrooms, reading, supervised play, making and community learning used by children from both surface and underground homes.
continuity_limits: Children retain ordinary routines and protected gathering areas; danger does not turn the school into a combat room.

areas.name: Care & Community Hall
areas.role: Clinic rooms, recovery, community meals and a separate kitchen wing, with independent clean and service circulation.
continuity_limits: Clinical rooms remain private. Kitchen noise and deliveries stay outside the care-room aisle.

areas.name: Central Lift & Stair Court
areas.role: A stacked neighborhood interchange at -12, -24 and -36 m, with ordinary lifts and independent stairs.
continuity_limits: This core has no direct surface entrance. It connects only the protected side of the underground town.

areas.name: Service Receiving Hall
areas.role: Freight from the workshop service passage is checked, staged and handed into the west neighborhood through a local closure.
continuity_limits: The dock gate is a separate surface-to-town defensive boundary; it cannot be left as an unguarded bypass.

areas.name: West Deep Warren
areas.role: A second residential neighborhood, equal in dignity and quality to the upper warren. Planning occupancy: 400 residents / 100 homes.
continuity_limits: Depth is not a class hierarchy. These residents use surface gardens, markets and celebrations daily.

areas.name: East Deep Warren
areas.role: Dense family courtyards, homes, doorstep shops and social galleries on the second inhabited level. Planning occupancy: 400 residents / 100 homes.
continuity_limits: The four wards are normal permanent homes, not temporary emergency beds.

areas.name: Deep Commons & Kitchens
areas.role: A shared meal hall, neighborhood shops and kitchens beside the lower residential streets.
continuity_limits: Keep food preparation, clean stores and waste handling distinct. Household kitchens also exist.

areas.name: Food Gardens & Grow Rooms
areas.role: Powered growing rooms, seed storage and food preparation for selected greens, herbs and plant starts.
continuity_limits: Grow lights require power. Underground cultivation supplements surface gardens and external trade; it does not feed everybody alone.

areas.name: Assembly & Refuge Hall
areas.role: Used daily for gatherings, sport, performances and clubs. In a protective state it receives surface residents, with rest, care and family reunification zones.
continuity_limits: 800 additional refuge places is a production planning target, not a certified capacity. Do not displace underground households to make refuge space.

areas.name: Baths & Laundry
areas.role: Shared baths, private washing rooms, laundry, drying and neighborhood maintenance stores.
continuity_limits: Separate clean water from drainage. No connection opens through the Welcome Hall above.

areas.name: Utility Repair Hall
areas.role: Maintainable local power distribution, battery rooms, spare equipment and repair benches.
continuity_limits: Separate zones can be isolated. A failure here cannot be written as an unexplained instant shutdown of all life support.

areas.name: Water & Air Service Rooms
areas.role: Partitioned potable reserve, wastewater lift plant, drainage sumps and air-handling rooms.
continuity_limits: Wastewater must be pumped up to the existing -3 m service level; it cannot flow uphill by gravity. Independent duty/backup equipment and local controls.

areas.name: Deep Stores
areas.role: Dry staples, household supplies, repair materials and documented community reserves.
continuity_limits: Stock quantities change in the event ledger. No infinite supplies or unearned emergency solution.

areas.name: West Stair & Refuge Core
areas.role: An independent protected stair/refuge core links all three underground levels to the surface service walk at (-210,-40,0).
continuity_limits: Outside entry is locally controlled. Occupants can leave from inside without network permission; surface conditions still determine whether evacuation is safe.

areas.name: East Stair & Refuge Core
areas.role: A second separated protected stair/refuge core links all levels to the surface service walk at (144,-40,0).
continuity_limits: This is a distinct route from the west core. Include it in any surface-overrun state and keep staff able to operate it locally.

services.air: Two separated intake/service paths, zoned air handlers, local dampers, monitoring and backup power. Daylight ducts are not ventilation calculations or person-sized access routes. Do not seal inhabited rooms without maintaining breathable air.
services.water: Independent covered potable reserve. Surface spring feed descends in sealed pipes; pressure control and branch isolation are local. Canal water remains separate.
services.waste: Sealed underground drains collect at -36 m. Duty/backup pumps lift wastewater to the established southeast service/treatment connection at -3 m. Emergency holding is local; no uphill gravity drain.
services.power: Local batteries and distributed supplies support emergency light, communications, air and pumps. A forged record cannot physically open a manual gate.
services.food: Surface gardens, traded staples, household stores and powered grow rooms all contribute. Refuge supplies are tracked finite stock.
services.daylight: Sealed light ducts at LW-W and LW-E serve upper street connectors. Lower streets use comfortable electric lighting and planted communal spaces; no invented sunlight below solid rock.

operating_states.rule: Outdoor East Gate and the main underground public entrance welcome normal public use. Inner closures stand open. Homes, clinics and service rooms retain normal privacy and staff access.
Stewards guide people inward, keep arrival routes legible, account for families and operate local gates only when the closure line is clear. Other entrances receive coordinated local closures.

The inhabited underground town remains behind IG-A / IG-B / SG-W and locally controlled stair thresholds. Compartment doors limit a local breach. Civilian refuge, air, water and egress remain operating priorities.
Inspect routes, verify both physical and digital records, reunite households and reopen by location. Record damage and repairs as dated overlays.

neighborhoods.name: Hearth Terraces
neighborhoods.identity: The outdoor neighborhood: laundry galleries, balcony conversations and shifting daylight. Surface homes are as permanent and socially important as the underground wards.
neighborhoods.look: Pale stone, slate, dark timber and individually colored doors; the established three tiers remain fixed.
neighborhoods.sound: Cloth moving in the breeze, footsteps on timber, distant market calls.
neighborhoods.rhythm: Early doors open toward the market; evening neighbors gather on galleries and make room for people returning from below.
neighborhoods.friction: A celebration on the gallery carries into someone else's early bedtime. Residents solve it with schedules, not blame.
neighborhoods.thread: Madger and Snow live here. Their doorway is private; being a founder does not make every hour public.

neighborhoods.name: West Lantern Warren
neighborhoods.identity: A sociable neighborhood of doorstep exchanges, mending and shared play. Lantern means ordinary warm lighting, not a power object.
neighborhoods.look: Honey plaster, green door panels and replaceable amber electric shades; clear street crossings and low shared benches.
neighborhoods.sound: A sewing treadle, a kettle, soft games and the arrival of bread carts.
neighborhoods.rhythm: Breakfast is lively; school departures clear the common street; quiet household work follows.
neighborhoods.friction: A generous neighbor volunteers another household's time without asking. An apology changes the arrangement.
neighborhoods.thread: Mara and Jun know the value of useful work but disagree about when a favor has become an obligation.

neighborhoods.name: East Orchard Warren
neighborhoods.identity: A neighborhood with a strong learning and gardening rhythm beside School & Play Hall. The name does not create an underground orchard or sunlight.
neighborhoods.look: Garden green, chalk blue, labeled plant starts under grow lights and picture-and-number door signs.
neighborhoods.sound: Practice counting, rolling school carts and watering cans returning to their rack.
neighborhoods.rhythm: Families share the morning school route; afternoons mix games, reading and plant care.
neighborhoods.friction: A confident child wants to finish a group project alone; an overlooked classmate has the useful observation.
neighborhoods.thread: Neri helps students investigate familiar places without turning every walk into a lesson.

neighborhoods.name: West Deep Warren
neighborhoods.identity: A quiet neighborhood with many shift workers, apprentices and makers. Residents work throughout the Burrow; this is not a compulsory worker district.
neighborhoods.look: Slate-blue doors, cream surrounds, soft wall lights and felt-backed notice strips; repairable furnishings show personal care.
neighborhoods.sound: Soft shoes, low conversation and a careful knock before visiting a resting household.
neighborhoods.rhythm: Meals and rest happen at different hours. Deliveries follow marked quiet periods.
neighborhoods.friction: An apprentice wants to display a new invention while a neighbor needs sleep. They find a daytime testing place.
neighborhoods.thread: Tavi learns that making something impressive and making it dependable are different achievements.

neighborhoods.name: East Deep Warren
neighborhoods.identity: A mixed-age neighborhood of communal suppers, small performances and storytelling, linked to Deep Commons.
neighborhoods.look: Terracotta door accents, cream walls, woven fabrics and small reversible displays made by residents.
neighborhoods.sound: Tableware, rehearsed harmonies, a story stopping when someone asks a question.
neighborhoods.rhythm: Afternoon meal preparation brings people out; performances end before the posted quiet period.
neighborhoods.friction: A familiar storyteller dislikes a younger resident correcting a detail. Evidence and kindness both matter.
neighborhoods.thread: Pell and Edda care for people in different ways: a correct record and an attentive conversation each have a place.

residents.name: Mara Reed
residents.want: Finish the morning bake on time and keep one afternoon free for drawing.
residents.strength: Remembers preferences and plans work well.
residents.flaw: Says yes before checking whether she has the time.
residents.relationship: Jun pushes her to name the true cost of a favor; Madger recognizes his own overcommitment in her.
residents.scene: She gives a child a counted delivery task and lets the child finish it.
residents.limit: Generosity does not create unlimited free stock. She can decline an extra order without becoming selfish.
residents.visual_note: Flour-marked oat apron, short green neck cloth, practical sleeves; final character model and voice remain unapproved.
residents.history_open: Origin, relatives, arrival date and first meeting with Madger remain unassigned.

residents.name: Tavi Moss
residents.want: Earn responsibility for a complete repair, not only the easy preparation.
residents.strength: Notices how parts fit and asks direct questions.
residents.flaw: Hides small mistakes while hoping to fix them before anyone notices.
residents.relationship: Gorilla White teaches without doing every task for him; Iona asks for measurements before confidence.
residents.scene: He marks a chair as unfinished instead of allowing it onto the loan shelf.
residents.limit: Skill grows through supervised work. He cannot improvise a life-support repair or a universal gadget.
residents.visual_note: Indigo work vest, rolled cuffs and a small repair notebook; model and voice are development notes.
residents.history_open: Family, apprenticeship start and reason for coming to the Burrow remain unassigned.

residents.name: Iona Flint
residents.want: Keep inspections boring enough that everyone else can enjoy the day.
residents.strength: Patient verification and excellent practical memory.
residents.flaw: Sometimes delivers a correct finding so bluntly that people stop listening.
residents.relationship: Bot helps compare records; she insists that a recorded reading and a physical reading are different things.
residents.scene: She invites a worried neighbor to see the relevant gauge and explains what it can and cannot show.
residents.limit: She is one member of a trained service team, not the sole person capable of keeping the town alive.
residents.visual_note: Copper cuff marker, slate work jacket and an ordinary tool roll; no magical blindness compensation.
residents.history_open: Training, former home and earlier service incidents remain unassigned.

residents.name: Neri Tern
residents.want: Help students ask better questions and leave room for their own answers.
residents.flaw: Overplans and can mistake an unexpected approach for a distraction.
residents.relationship: Snow helps children practice patient observation; Neri respects that Snow is a dog, not a speaking classroom prop.
residents.scene: She changes a lesson when a student notices that the delivery map is hard to read.
residents.limit: Children are not used as covert investigators or put in danger to prove maturity.
residents.visual_note: Chalk-blue overshirt, cream satchel and pockets for reusable cards; final model and voice remain open.
residents.history_open: Education, birthplace and why she chose teaching here remain unassigned.

residents.name: Pell Fen
residents.want: Make a newcomer's first day understandable.
residents.flaw: Clings to a procedure when the procedure itself is confusing someone.
residents.relationship: Madger encourages a personal welcome; Bot helps Pell explain rather than merely repeat a rule.
residents.scene: Pell walks a visitor to the correct counter instead of pointing at another form.
residents.limit: Public access is not a personality test. A visitor is not suspicious just because they are unfamiliar.
residents.visual_note: Small green steward tab, cream waistcoat and a simple map folder; no fortress-guard uniform.
residents.history_open: Arrival, earlier loyalties and any founding-era role remain unassigned.

residents.name: Jun Ash
residents.role: Mender, sign painter and public-notice contributor
residents.want: Make useful objects beautiful and make important information easy to find.
residents.strength: Detail, economy of material and a sharp eye for inconsistency.
residents.flaw: Treats an imperfect finished piece as a personal failure.
residents.relationship: Mara values a practical repair; Jun learns to accept visible seams instead of hiding every repair.
residents.scene: Jun adds a picture and a floor number to a sign that previously relied on color alone.

residents.history_open: Family craft traditions and the meaning of any personal keepsake remain unassigned.

residents.name: Edda Brook
residents.want: Give people a safe place to recover without making them feel like a burden.
residents.strength: Listening, organization and firm practical boundaries.
residents.flaw: Finds it easier to ask others to rest than to rest herself.
residents.relationship: Gorilla White cannot persuade her that endurance cancels recovery; she also accepts help from him.
residents.scene: She asks an injured neighbor whom they want informed, then records the agreed handoff.
residents.limit: Care is confidential. Treatment is not instant magic, and she does not diagnose everyone by looking at them.

residents.history_open: Training, family and previous rescue experiences remain unassigned.

residents.name: Sori Wren
residents.want: Get good food to tables while preserving seed and spare stock for the next cycle.

residents.flaw: Hears criticism of a harvest as criticism of personal worth.
residents.relationship: Iona and Sori sometimes disagree about allocation, then compare actual supply and need.

chapters.title: A place worth returning to
chapters.lead: The Burrow is a shared home before it becomes the setting of an adventure.

sections.title: One town, several ways of living
sections.text: Outdoor terraces hold markets, gardens and homes. Two underground levels hold permanent neighborhoods, schools, shops and shared meals. Residents move between them for work, friendship and leisure. Neither part is a lesser home.

sections.title: What this edition fixes
sections.text: Every existing footprint, route, level and crossing is retained. Seven detailed sub-plans fit inside allocated spaces. Eight recurring residents, neighborhood identities and everyday institutions give those spaces a social life.

sections.title: What the owner has established
sections.text: Madger created or founded the Burrow. This does not mean he rules it or built every part alone. Why he founded it, the condition of the site beforehand and who joined him remain questions for the history phase.

sections.title: Present fact, history, and possibility
sections.text: Present-day entries can be used now. History reservations are questions, not hidden answers. Story seeds are possible conflicts, not events that have already happened. Concept art establishes atmosphere; measured plans control placement.

chapters.title: Five neighborhoods, one community
chapters.lead: Residents have local habits without becoming stereotypes of their address.

chapters.title: The ordinary day has a shape
chapters.lead: Time is tracked by the surface day. Underground lighting and quiet periods follow it, while essential services work in shifts.

sections.title: Before breakfast
sections.text: Receiving teams count goods. Kitchen shifts prepare bread and meals. Maintenance teams compare local readings. Early deliveries stay on work routes and avoid sleeping galleries.

sections.title: Morning
sections.text: Families leave homes above and below. Children and guardians travel toward UG-06; adults go to gardens, shops and workshops. Visitors enter through the public arrival sequence. Nobody must pass through a private home to reach a civic place.

sections.title: Midday
sections.text: The surface market and Underhall share the busiest exchanges. Shared kitchens supplement household kitchens. Tables make room for people who are eating alone as well as established groups.

sections.title: Afternoon
sections.text: Learning clubs, repairs and personal errands overlap. Service staff hand over unfinished tasks. School is not the only place children appear, and work is not the only activity adults have.

sections.title: Evening
sections.text: People return to different neighborhoods, cook, rehearse, read and visit. The outdoor gate can close routinely after an announced last entry; underground inner gates stay open unless a protective state is explicitly declared.

sections.title: Night
sections.text: Quiet does not mean abandoned. Limited service shifts continue, routes remain legible and home privacy matters. Night staff take rest later; daylight characters cannot appear everywhere without time passing.

chapters.title: How the community makes decisions
chapters.lead: Madger brings people together. The town also works when he is absent, tired or wrong.

sections.title: The Common Table
sections.text: Residents raise matters at BRW-02 or scheduled UG-14 assemblies. Neighborhood stewards and service leads explain their part; a rotating facilitator keeps the discussion usable. Decisions and reasons are recorded where residents can inspect them.

sections.title: Ordinary rights
sections.text: People can ask questions, correct a record, decline an optional activity and keep their home private. Welcome, basic care and refuge do not depend on a wallet, rank, species or personal friendship with a hero.

sections.title: Work has accountable owners
sections.text: Service teams own schedules and handoffs. One named person leads a shift, but another can take over. The Records House preserves evidence and corrections; it does not silently become the government.

sections.title: Disagreement without an enemy
sections.text: A grower, a teacher and a repair team can reasonably want the same cart or timeslot. Show the actual constraint, listen to affected people and record the compromise. A losing suggestion does not make its owner disloyal.

sections.title: Urgent decisions
sections.text: A local lead can respond to immediate danger within an established role. Gate and service changes are logged and reviewed afterward. Urgency is temporary responsibility, not permanent power.

sections.title: The founder's place
sections.text: Madger has influence through trust and action, not a private veto. His developing leadership is visible when he accepts a good objection and helps someone else carry a decision through.

chapters.title: Work, exchange and finite resources
chapters.lead: The town is prosperous because useful work is shared, maintained and recorded.

sections.title: A household economy
sections.text: Residents exchange goods and paid work, share some resources and volunteer by choice. Use ordinary prices, tickets and receipts when a scene needs them. Currency names, exchange rates and any relationship to real-world MADGER products remain unassigned.

sections.title: Food takes several routes
sections.text: Surface gardens and powered grow rooms supply part of the food. Trade brings grain and other staples; stores buffer interruptions. Household cooking and common kitchens coexist. The Bread Counter receives prepared batches from UG-12 rather than adding an unplanned oven shaft.

sections.title: Repair has a queue
sections.text: A repair ticket records item, owner, fault, promised next update and current status. Loan tools have a return record. A delay can be honest; hiding it creates a relationship problem before it becomes a safety problem.

sections.title: Shared resources need boundaries
sections.text: Communal does not mean ownerless. A household's keepsake is not quest loot. Lending a cart needs consent and a return time. Essential service stock is separate from a decorative project budget.

sections.title: Local consequences first
sections.text: A missing flour crate affects named orders and a meal plan. A failed grow light affects a room and its crop schedule. State the reserve and the alternative before escalating to a town-wide crisis.

sections.title: Rest is part of capacity
sections.text: Staff rotations, apprentices and handoffs are visible. Gorilla cannot lift every object, Bot cannot inspect every log and Edda cannot remain on duty forever. Ordinary neighbors keep things running.

chapters.title: Culture you can see and hear
chapters.lead: The Burrow feels like one place through recurring details, not identical buildings or identical residents.

sections.title: A repair is allowed to show
sections.text: A neat seam, a replaced chair rung and a dated bridge repair can be visible. Makers receive credit. This supports pride in care without implying an ancient tradition or founding legend that has not been written.

sections.title: Courtesy at a threshold
sections.text: Knock, wait and ask before entering. Leave the common street clear. Return borrowed objects to the agreed place. Visitors can learn these habits through a friendly interaction instead of a lecture.

sections.title: Meals and celebrations
sections.text: Shared tables welcome newcomers; participation is optional. Bridge Reopening Day is a specific present event, not yet an annual founding festival. Small performances, games and skill exchanges need no catastrophe to justify an episode.

sections.title: Readable places
sections.text: Combine area number, word and simple symbol. Color helps but is never the only direction cue. Workshop tools are labeled; school notices use pictures; light levels change gently along public routes.

sections.title: A controlled sound palette
sections.text: Surface scenes carry wind, water, wheel movement and market calls. Underground scenes carry close footsteps, tableware, soft mechanical ventilation and household sounds. No constant ominous drone under a happy town.

sections.title: People and animals
sections.text: This edition adds person-like animal residents without changing Snow's identity as an ordinary adult dog. Final population biology and species histories remain open. Appearance does not determine honesty, intelligence or allegiance.

chapters.title: Neighbors with work of their own
chapters.lead: Present-day roles are authored additions. Birthplaces, arrival stories, ages in years and family histories remain open.

chapters.title: Neighbors beyond the heroes
chapters.lead: These residents can disagree, be funny, make errors and change without every story making them a villain or victim.

chapters.title: Four heroes in a larger town
chapters.lead: The existing hero arcs stay intact. Their growth appears through choices that affect other people.

sections.title: Madger / belonging without control
sections.text: He starts things and makes introductions. Mara reflects his habit of saying yes to too much; Pell shows how welcome can work through an ordinary system. Progress means entrusting a meaningful task, accepting a refusal and sharing credit.

sections.title: Gorilla White / strength that teaches
sections.text: The workshop is shared. Tavi needs a chance to finish a job, and Edda expects Gorilla to rest when necessary. Progress means demonstrating a skill, letting someone else try and receiving protection without shame.

sections.title: MADGER Bot / usefulness without certainty
sections.text: Iona compares physical readings; Pell sees the person behind a record. Bot can preserve conflicting evidence without inventing an answer. Progress means marking uncertainty clearly and explaining the limits of his access.

sections.title: Snow White / attention that connects
sections.text: Her actions are canine: sniffing, listening, pausing, looking back, returning and resting. Neri and the children learn to wait for a clear indication. Snow never translates a scent into a spoken explanation or detects a digital packet.

sections.title: Friendship has reciprocal care
sections.text: A tired friend receives help. A disagreement is resolved by changed conduct, not merely a speech. The team shares ordinary meals and jokes so later separation or danger has an established emotional cost.

sections.title: Not every hero in every scene
sections.text: Episodes can focus on one or two relationships while preserving the others' whereabouts. The pilot still includes all four; its brief runtime does not require introductions for all eight new residents.

chapters.title: Underhall is a real address
chapters.lead: Four named north-side shops now occupy existing bays. Their customers and deliveries share the public square; no exterior wall or main corridor moves.

chapters.title: Mara's Bread Counter
chapters.lead: A small shop with counted bread stock, a pickup counter and room to queue off the public crossing.

chapters.title: Repair & Tool Loan
chapters.lead: A neighborhood handoff point for small repairs and loan tools. Large or hazardous work goes to BRW-07.

chapters.title: Pantry & Produce
chapters.lead: A measured neighborhood supply shop for fresh produce, dry staples and household containers.

chapters.title: Jun's Mending Room
chapters.lead: Mending, fitting and small sign work, with a clear private fitting area and visible pickup rack.

chapters.title: Learning Room One
chapters.lead: One of the four already allocated learning rooms, for a flexible group of about 16 learners. Other rooms and shifts share the school demand.

chapters.title: Care Room One
chapters.lead: A private assessment and recovery room within the already allocated clinic zone, with a quiet waiting position and handwash point.

chapters.title: Lantern Street Home 001
chapters.lead: A compact 48 m2 household home within the southwest frontage of the northwest court. It is one of the ward's 100 planned homes, not an extra unit.

chapters.title: Safety is a condition, not a color
chapters.lead: A place can be welcoming, private, supervised or temporarily unsafe. Keep access rules separate from threat level.

sections.title: Everyday civic spaces
sections.text: Markets, commons, school routes, clinic waiting areas and the assembly hall are maintained safe in the peaceful baseline. Minor friction is social or practical; the background does not randomly attack residents.

sections.title: Private spaces
sections.text: Homes and personal records are private, not dangerous. A closed bedroom door is a boundary, not automatic evidence of a secret. Ask who has permission and why.

sections.title: Working spaces
sections.text: A running wheel, hot kitchen, tool bench, wet floor or service plant can present an ordinary local hazard. Supervision and a clear work boundary make the risk understandable without making the whole district sinister.

sections.title: Temporary restricted areas
sections.text: Inspection, repair, smoke or a blocked route can change one location's status. Record start, reason, affected paths, alternate route and conditions for reopening. Restore or preserve damage explicitly.

sections.title: Surface overrun
sections.text: The welcome sequence, inner closures, service boundary and stair thresholds keep their v2 roles. The town's response is protection of people and lifelines. No extra escape tunnel appears simply because a scene needs one.

sections.title: Dangerous regions come later
sections.text: No named wilderness, monster territory, hostile settlement or attacker base is established here. Those places will need their own geography, ecology, history, inhabitants and connection to the Burrow before use.

chapters.title: Lifelines and trust
chapters.lead: Separate physical events, digital records and what characters believe happened.

sections.title: Water and air
sections.text: Iona's team checks local conditions; records help compare them. Drinking water stays separate from the canal. Underground waste is pumped up to the established service connection. Doors do not make air, pumps or staff unnecessary.

sections.title: Power and food
sections.text: Local supplies and backups have limited capacity. The wheel, roofs and batteries are not one omnipotent core. Grow rooms need power. Food reserves require quantities and elapsed time before a shortage becomes a plot fact.

sections.title: A receipt is a claim
sections.text: D17 remains a delivery identifier. A duplicate could reflect error, replay, fraud or another cause not yet established. The pilot does not decide which. Bot preserves source, time and uncertainty rather than accusing a visitor.

sections.title: Physical controls remain physical
sections.text: A forged status cannot move a manual gate bar. A later antagonist must have a documented route, ability, access and limit. Do not replace a mystery with a universal hacking power.

sections.title: Private information has purpose
sections.text: A service reading, a delivery record and a care record have different viewers. Residents can request corrections. No omniscient surveillance wall is added to simplify exposition.

sections.title: Repair creates history
sections.text: When a later event changes a sign, door, service setting or relationship, record its before and after. The next episode inherits that result instead of resetting the town for convenience.

chapters.title: Many kinds of episode can live here
chapters.lead: These are story seeds, not completed events or locked episode orders.

sections.title: Community comedy / a favor too many
sections.text: Mara promises more orders than one shift can finish. Madger's attempt to help creates a second commitment. A truthful renegotiation lets others plan; the cost is awkwardness and work, not a surprise villain.

sections.title: Craft / the unfinished chair
sections.text: Tavi wants a visible success. A repair looks finished but still fails an ordinary check. He must label it honestly and ask for help before a neighbor uses it.

sections.title: Learning / the map that misleads
sections.text: Neri's group tests a wayfinding card. Jun discovers it depends on color and an adult's reading height. A clearer sign helps visitors and changes Neri's planned lesson.

sections.title: Friendship / the empty place at supper
sections.text: Gorilla misses a shared meal because everyone assumes he can finish one more job. The others must notice the habit, not just deliver a plate. He must also name his own limit.

sections.title: Mystery / two records, one crate
sections.text: A delivery count disagrees with a stored receipt. Bot and Pell separate what is known from what is guessed. A local discrepancy supports investigation without deciding the season villain in advance.

sections.title: Weather, care and defense later
sections.text: A seasonal disruption can require a route change; a recovery story can test patience; an eventual defense story can test welcome under pressure. Each uses known places, bounded abilities and lasting consequences.

chapters.title: The pilot still begins with joy
chapters.lead: The audience should care about ordinary life before it notices the first discrepancy.

sections.title: 00:00-00:50 / home, street, sunlight
sections.text: Begin in an underground household and Underhall. Follow ordinary movement up to the surface. All four heroes contribute through brief useful actions. Do not open on alarms, fortifications or a lore monologue.

sections.title: 00:50-01:40 / a welcome
sections.text: A visitor and delivery show public access. Inner gates stand open. One duplicate D17 receipt is quietly preserved. Use inward framing at the outdoor threshold so exterior geography stays unassigned.

sections.title: 01:40-03:00 / shared accomplishment
sections.text: Neighbors reopen the weather-repaired bridge. Gorilla accepts help; Madger shares credit. The bridge remains sound. Allow real route changes and time cuts between locations.

sections.title: 03:00-04:10 / life continues
sections.text: Learning, food and a small personal exchange keep the town alive. After a time cut, Snow holds an indication at the intact gate relay. This is a physical trace with no known cause.

sections.title: 04:10-05:00 / homeward, then a question
sections.text: Friends and households return home. Establish routine evening gate closing before the final unexplained acknowledgment. No one has passed. End with a small contradiction, not an attacker reveal.

sections.title: What the new cast contributes
sections.text: One or two recurring residents may have readable supporting actions; others remain background or offscreen. Avoid using five minutes to explain eight biographies. Their deeper stories belong in later episodes.

chapters.title: Build history from evidence and choices
chapters.lead: The present world is now detailed enough to ask specific historical questions without filling the answers prematurely.

sections.title: Madger and the founding
sections.text: Owner-established fact: Madger created the Burrow. Still open: what he wanted to protect or provide, what existed at the site, the first commitment he made, who disagreed, what he sacrificed and how shared responsibility grew.

sections.title: The four companions
sections.text: For each pair: where they first met, what each wanted, the initial misunderstanding, the action that earned trust and the unresolved difference that survives today. Establish order and elapsed time before writing flashbacks.

sections.title: The residents' origins
sections.text: Track former home, reason for leaving or staying, skills brought, people left behind, arrival route and present sense of belonging. Not every resident must be a refugee or share one founding trauma.

sections.title: Every place has a material history
sections.text: For each area: prior condition, builder or community, purpose at creation, source of materials, later alterations and surviving evidence. Do not date a door, trophy or inscription until its event is recorded.

sections.title: What is true versus remembered
sections.text: Maintain objective event, eyewitness accounts, rumor and character belief separately. A mistaken memory can be dramatic; it must not silently alter the factual ledger.

sections.title: Chronology before flashbacks
sections.text: Use relative sequence IDs until calendar and character ages are fixed. Give an event prerequisites, location, participants, result and who knows. Then connect it to the already established present.

chapters.title: Make future threats belong to this world
chapters.lead: Villains, monsters and hostile animals will be developed in the history and wider-world phase, with reasons, limits and consequences.

sections.title: An antagonist is more than an attack
sections.text: Reserve fields for desire, belief, grievance, chosen methods, resources, limits, relationships and a line they will or will not cross. Explain what they want from the Burrow and why they cannot simply take it.

sections.title: Species is not allegiance
sections.text: An evil animal can be an individual who makes cruel choices. A dangerous predator can act through hunger or territory. Keep moral choice, ecological danger and any later supernatural influence distinct.

sections.title: A creature belongs somewhere
sections.text: Define habitat, food, movement, senses, reproduction if relevant, signs of presence and interaction with other life. Establish what residents know before an encounter. Powers need visible limits and costs.

sections.title: Safe and dangerous are contextual
sections.text: A home refuge can be safe for residents; a nesting area can be dangerous to an intruder without being evil. Map boundaries and routes. A monster does not appear in a neighborhood merely because an action scene is due.

sections.title: Mystery is not a premature answer
sections.text: No villain identity, monster species, magical system or exterior map is fixed by this edition. The D17 record and Snow's trace remain unresolved; neither is retroactively declared proof of a creature or faction.

sections.title: Reveal in stages
sections.text: A later story may progress from observation to competing explanations, a verified local effect, a responsible actor and wider stakes. Each revelation must explain prior evidence and leave the characters with a meaningful choice.

chapters.title: A world that can carry seasons
chapters.lead: A season should change relationships and knowledge while preserving a recognizable home.

sections.title: Choose one central question
sections.text: Examples for future development: Can a welcoming community protect itself without losing trust? When does helping become control? What does belonging require from a founder and from a newcomer? These are possibilities, not a locked season plan.

sections.title: Give each episode a complete local story
sections.text: A person wants something in a specific place. A real constraint forces a choice. That choice has a visible cost or benefit. The episode resolves its local question while leaving a consequence another story can use.

sections.title: Track parallel arcs
sections.text: For each hero record present belief, test, choice, changed behavior and relationship effect. Use small differences across episodes. A speech without a changed action is not an earned arc.

sections.title: Limit exposition
sections.text: Let recurring signs, places and habits carry familiarity. Introduce an origin detail only when it affects a current decision. A history volume can be extensive while an episode reveals only what that moment needs.

sections.title: Separate story and game states
sections.text: Player upgrades, collectibles and retries do not become historical facts automatically. The same place keeps its coordinates. An anime background and a game room agree on doors, travel connections and permanent objects.

sections.title: Before a scene is approved
sections.text: Check location and access state, time and travel, who knows what, resources and injuries, approved likenesses and voices, physical limits, and the event ledger. Snow remains canine. Madger keeps normal teeth and a clean face.

chapters.title: What is now ready to use
chapters.lead: This is an additive present-day expansion. It does not move the Burrow or silently write its past.

sections.title: Seven detailed spaces
sections.text: UG-03-S01 Bread Counter; S02 Repair & Tool Loan; S03 Pantry & Produce; S04 Mending Room; UG-06-R01 Learning Room One; UG-07-R01 Care Room One; UG-04-H001 Lantern Street Home 001. Every footprint stays inside its existing parent allocation.

sections.title: Five neighborhoods and eight neighbors
sections.text: The original surface neighborhood and four underground wards now have distinct daily identities. Eight resident dossiers record present roles, desires, strengths, flaws and relationships, with historical fields intentionally open.

sections.title: What stays unchanged
sections.text: All 37 primary area positions and footprints, the surface and underground route graphs, three canal crossings, four approved hero profiles and voice references, 2,400-resident planning baseline, public access and independent inner defense.

sections.title: What remains to develop
sections.text: The other household interiors, complete occupancy census, final civilian model sheets and voices, detailed founding chronology, companion meetings, migrations, factions, named villains, monsters and exterior regions.

sections.title: Source of authority
sections.text: Latest owner instructions come first. Current canon and measured plans control the world; event records control changes. This volume adds present-day detail and records future questions. The atmosphere painting is not a measured camera plate.

sections.title: Use across media
sections.text: The edition supplies stable addresses and relationships for comics, videos, episodes, seasons and game scenes. It is world development material; it does not claim those media have already been produced.
